Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

go to the dogs phrase

also they’re going to the dogs, go to ruin, go to pot, go downhill, things are going downhill

classical

Plaut. Cist. 2.1.12; Tac. A. 1.79 (Lewis & Short s.v. pessum)
Traupman 97
Traupman 305

pessum īre

go to the dogs, go to ruin

Pessum, “to the bottom”, lives on in a few phrases, mostly early and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short). To ruin something is pessum dare.

Other words

  • inclīnāta rēs est — things are going downhill

    also used · modern · Traupman 97; Traupman 306

    Traupman’s phrase, “the affair has tilted”. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

Examples

  • pessum itūrōs fēcundissimōs Italiae campōs

    that the most fertile plains of Italy would go to ruinTac. A. 1.79 (Lewis & Short)

  • Pessum eunt.

    They’re going to the dogs.Traupman 97
